canonical_fact: JAM's authorization system separates the acquisition and assignment of coretime from the exact work package that later consumes it.
misconceptions: The entity that purchases coretime must also construct every work package that uses it.

relations.statement: Authorizers are the executable policy mechanism of the authorization system.

title: Authorization system

canonical_fact: An authorizer is bounded PVM logic that decides whether a work package, including its token, is permitted to execute on a particular core and yields a trace on success.
misconceptions: An authorizer is an on-chain governance vote rather than executable PVM logic.

relations.statement: An authorizer interprets the work package’s opaque authorization token.
A successful authorizer execution emits an authorization trace.

title: Authorizer

canonical_fact: An authorization token is opaque data carried by a work package and interpreted by the authorizer as part of the authorization decision.
misconceptions: An authorization token has protocol-wide fixed semantics independent of the authorizer.
title: Authorization token

canonical_fact: An authorization trace is opaque output produced by a successful authorizer execution to characterize the authorization outcome.
title: Authorization trace

canonical_fact: An authorizer's configuration is opaque data combined with the authorizer code hash to identify the authorizer instance.
title: Authorizer configuration

canonical_fact: An authorizer is identified by hashing its PVM code hash together with its configuration blob.
title: Authorizer identity

canonical_fact: Each core has an authorizer pool containing the authorizer identities currently allowable for work on that core.
misconceptions: There is one global authorizer pool shared by all cores.

relations.statement: Each core’s authorizer queue replenishes its authorizer pool.

title: Authorizer pool

canonical_fact: Each core has a fixed-size authorizer queue used to replenish its authorizer pool over time.
title: Authorizer queue

canonical_fact: The authorizer queue is changed through accumulation by the appropriately privileged per-core assigner service rather than directly by arbitrary work packages.

relations.statement: Only the appropriately privileged per-core assigner may alter the authorizer queue through accumulation.

title: Authorizer queue mutation

canonical_fact: When a guaranteed work report consumes an authorizer for a core, the corresponding authorizer is removed from the core's pool as the pool transitions.
title: Used authorizer removal
